sources.title: Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut

stories.headline: Anthropic makes its Nasdaq debut, putting AI to a Wall Street test
stories.dek: Reuters calls the listing historic, framing the Claude maker's first day of trading as a test of AI's promise and peril.
stories.body:
Anthropic, the company behind the Claude family of AI models, has made its debut on the Nasdaq, according to Reuters. The news agency describes the listing as historic and frames it as a test of how public markets weigh both the promise and the peril of artificial intelligence.

Reuters published its report on November 19. Its framing positions the listing as more than a single company going public. It treats the debut as a referendum on how investors value frontier AI developers, which spend heavily on compute and research.

The listing drew heavy attention among developers. A Hacker News thread on the debut passed 1,000 points and collected more than 2,000 comments within a day.

Anthropic sells its Claude models to consumers, businesses and developers through its apps and API. Trading as a public company brings regular financial disclosure and quarterly scrutiny from shareholders. That is a different footing from the private funding rounds that have financed the large AI labs so far.

The first days of trading will show how the market prices the company. Further details on the listing, including the share price and valuation, will come from the trading record and Anthropic's own filings.
key_points: Anthropic has debuted on the Nasdaq, Reuters reports
Reuters calls the listing historic
Debut framed as a Wall Street test of AI's promise and peril
Hacker News thread passed 2,000 comments
stories.why_it_matters: A public Anthropic faces quarterly pressure from shareholders, which could shape Claude's pricing, API terms and product priorities for the developers who build on it.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day Flaw Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication

stories.headline: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited by Chinese hackers
stories.dek: A 9.8-rated authentication bypass in vCenter Server was used in espionage attacks for over two months before Broadcom shipped a fix.
stories.body:
Broadcom has released emergency updates for a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass that, according to Google's Mandiant, a suspected Chinese state-sponsored group exploited as a zero-day since early September 2026. The flaw, CVE-2026-123890, is rated 9.8 on the CVSS scale and sits in the VMware Directory Service.

Broadcom says an unauthenticated attacker with network access can bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. Mandiant explains that exploitation creates a session as administrator@vsphere.local, giving control over the virtual machines vCenter manages. The fix shipped November 19 in advisory VMSA-2026-0009, which Broadcom classifies as an emergency change. There is no official workaround, though network restrictions and firewall rules can reduce exposure.

The Hacker News reports the bug affects vCenter 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1, plus builds inside VMware Cloud Foundation, including the older 5.x line, vSphere Foundation and the Telco Cloud products. Enhanced Linked Mode makes no difference. Broadcom says vSphere 6.5, 6.7 and 7.0 should be presumed affected; 7.0 customers can request a patch under extended support. ESX itself is not affected. The updates are cumulative and cannot be applied through vCenter Quick Patch, and installing vCenter 8.0 U3m or 9.0.2.0200 blocks a later upgrade to Cloud Foundation 9.1.1.

Broadcom has not confirmed exploitation, but Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group tie the attacks to Armory Castle, formerly UNC5221, known for hitting Citrix NetScaler and Ivanti devices. BleepingComputer reports the group first broke in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, CVE-2026-102764, then moved to internal Linux systems. It used a custom Go tool called BONESAW to create a vCenter SSO admin account, steal the directory database and extract SAML signing keys. A second tool, SAWSNAKE, enabled Golden SAML attacks that bypass multifactor authentication. The attackers reached ESXi hosts and pulled Active Directory database files from virtual machines.

It is the second 9.8-rated bypass in the same component this year, after CVE-2026-59309 in July. The advisory also fixes four lower-severity bugs in SDDC Manager and VMware Tools for Windows.
key_points: CVE-2026-123890 rated 9.8, exploited as zero-day since early September
Patched November 19 in VMSA-2026-0009, no official workaround
Mandiant links attacks to suspected Chinese group Armory Castle
Affects vCenter 8.0, 9.0, 9.1; older vSphere presumed vulnerable
stories.why_it_matters: Anyone running vCenter in a homelab or at work should patch now, and plan around the Quick Patch limitation and the Cloud Foundation 9.1.1 upgrade conflict.

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: OpenSSL: Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)

stories.headline: OpenSSL patches 9.8-rated buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock()
stories.dek: A fix for CVE-2026-121481 targets the master, 4.0 and 4.1 branches and hardens the matching base64 decode function too.
stories.body:
OpenSSL is fixing a buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock(), its base64 encoding function. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-121481 and carries a CVSS score of 9.8, according to its Hacker News listing. The fix sits in pull request 33652 on GitHub.

The pull request is labeled for the master branch and for the openssl-4.0 and openssl-4.1 branches. The labels were added on November 11, 2026. That points to the 4.x release lines as the affected code.

The approach changed during review. An earlier version of the patch made EVP_EncodeBlock() return -1 for invalid inputs. Later commit messages describe a stricter fix: the function now calls OPENSSL_assert() for inputs that lead to undefined behavior. In practice that means a hard stop rather than an error code the caller might ignore.

The same guard is applied to EVP_DecodeBlock(), the decoding counterpart. The patch also fixes an incorrect length check in the base64encode() function in http_client.c. It updates the documentation and adds new tests that document existing behavior for zero-length inputs.

Outside work is already probing the area. On November 20, a commit to a fuzzing project referenced the pull request. It compares OpenSSL 4.x's AVX2 base64 encoder against the scalar path through the public API, using a decode round trip as a second check.

Applications that call EVP_EncodeBlock() or EVP_DecodeBlock() directly should watch for patched 4.0 and 4.1 builds. Code that passes unusual input lengths may now abort instead of returning.
key_points: CVE-2026-121481 is a buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock(), CVSS 9.8
Fix targets OpenSSL master, 4.0 and 4.1 branches
Invalid inputs now trigger OPENSSL_assert(); EVP_DecodeBlock() gets the same guard
Incorrect length check in http_client.c base64encode() also fixed
stories.why_it_matters: Anything linking OpenSSL 4.x and doing base64 through the EVP API needs the patched build. Code feeding bad lengths will now crash on an assert instead of silently overflowing.

cover.caption: CVSS score for the EVP_EncodeBlock() buffer overflow

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: UK government forced to admit it issued Apple a secret encryption order

stories.headline: UK must admit it sent Apple a secret encryption order, tribunal rules
stories.dek: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the government's neither-confirm-nor-deny stance, though the order's lawfulness and technical demands remain untested.
stories.body:
The UK's Investigatory Powers Tribunal has ruled that the government must acknowledge it issued Apple a Technical Capability Notice under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016. According to Reuters, the tribunal found the government had "not established that it would be damaging to national security" to confirm the order exists. Civil rights groups Liberty and Privacy International had challenged the secrecy, with their lawyer Ben Jaffey KC comparing it to the "emperor's new clothes."

The ruling does not decide whether the order is lawful or reveal what it requires. The Washington Post reported in February 2025 that the UK demanded backdoor access to encrypted iCloud data worldwide. Apple responded by pulling Advanced Data Protection for new UK users. A second notice, reportedly limited to British users, followed. A substantive hearing is expected in 2027.
key_points: The tribunal ruled the UK government must confirm it issued Apple a Technical Capability Notice.
The ruling does not address whether the order is lawful or what it demands of Apple.
Apple's legal challenge and one by Liberty and Privacy International face a substantive hearing expected in 2027.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution

stories.headline: PHP patches 18 flaws, including critical remote code execution bugs
stories.dek: Updates for PHP 8.2 through 8.5 follow Wednesday's advance warning; the worst bugs hit servers with non-default or uncommon setups.
stories.body:
The PHP team has shipped security updates fixing 18 vulnerabilities across all supported branches, including critical bugs that could let unauthenticated attackers run code on servers, BleepingComputer reports. PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 arrived Thursday, a day after the PHP security team warned that fixes were coming.

The most serious is CVE-2026-129289, a PHP-FPM request smuggling flaw rated 9.2 on the CVSS scale. It affects front ends that reuse backend connections, such as nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on, according to The Hacker News. Standard nginx and Apache configurations are not affected. The PHP team says all critical issues require non-default configuration or uncommon setups.

Admins who can't patch right away can disable persistent backend connections and set session.upload_progress.enabled=0. Security firm Aikido warns those steps don't cover every fix.
key_points: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 fix 18 CVEs, several rated critical with CVSS 9.2.
CVE-2026-129289 enables unauthenticated code execution on PHP-FPM setups that reuse backend connections.
Third-party maintainer Ondrej Surý has released patched packages for unsupported versions back to PHP 5.6.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: New Windows 11 lock screen zero-day unlocks BitLocker-protected PCs with just a few keystrokes

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It

stories.headline: Windows lock screen zero-day FastUnlock lets intruders run programs
stories.dek: The unpatched flaw abuses Narrator from the lock screen, and BitLocker in its default TPM-only mode offers no protection against it.
stories.body:
An unpatched Windows zero-day called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access to a locked PC start programs without signing in. Researcher Abdelhamid Naceri, known as Nightmare Eclipse, disclosed it this week. Endpoint-security firm ThreatLocker tested it the same day and confirmed it works, The Hacker News reports. Microsoft has no fix yet, and there is no sign of real-world attacks.

The trick uses "Forgot my PIN" and the Narrator screen reader to reach Settings behind the lock screen. Tom's Hardware says this could allow USB payloads or new admin accounts. ThreatLocker's test, however, only reached a limited, non-administrator account.

BitLocker does not stop it in its common TPM-only setup, because the drive is already unlocked when the lock screen appears. A BitLocker startup PIN, plus shutting down or hibernating machines, is the recommended defense.
key_points: FastUnlock requires physical access and uses Narrator to bypass the Windows lock screen; no patch exists yet.
ThreatLocker confirmed it works but reached only a limited, non-admin account; Tom's Hardware describes broader admin-account abuse.
A BitLocker startup PIN and shutting down or hibernating devices are the recommended mitigations.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: Intel 18A yields hit 70% as company signs Microsoft as EMIB customer

stories.headline: Intel says 18A yields hit 70 percent as Microsoft signs on for EMIB
stories.dek: Microsoft also locks in multi-year Xeon supply, including next-generation Diamond Rapids chips, though volumes and financial terms remain undisclosed.
stories.body:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Thursday that yields on the company's 18A (1.8nm-class) process have reached 70 percent. "When I took over, 18A yield was horrible; now we are at 70%," Tan said at the TomorrowX conference. He did not say which yield metric he meant. Tom's Hardware calls the figure decent for this stage of the ramp.

Intel also signed a long-term deal with Microsoft. Microsoft secures multi-year Xeon supply, including next-generation Diamond Rapids chips, and will use Intel's EMIB packaging for in-house multi-chiplet data center silicon. Tom's Hardware says Microsoft is the first company to publicly commit to EMIB. The announcement names no processors, volumes, schedules or financial terms.

18A already builds Panther Lake compute tiles and Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest chiplets. The two companies are also jointly developing CXL memory expansion, QAT acceleration and TDX security.
key_points: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says 18A yields have reached 70 percent, without specifying the yield metric.
Microsoft signs multi-year Xeon supply deal including Diamond Rapids, with no volumes or terms disclosed.
Microsoft is the first company to publicly commit to Intel's EMIB packaging for its own silicon.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: DDR6 RAM shrinks by 44% while delivering 4 times more bandwidth than DDR5 — JEDEC previews 12.8 GT/s modules with up to 1 terabyte of capacity per slot

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: DDR6 memory modules to be almost half the size of DDR5 and almost double the max speed

stories.headline: JEDEC previews DDR6: 74mm modules starting at 12.8 GT/s
stories.dek: The standards body says DDR6 is built for the data center first, with a 96-bit bus and no official launch date yet.
stories.body:
JEDEC has published a preview of the DDR6 memory specification. Modules shrink to 74mm, 44 percent shorter than DDR5's 133mm sticks. Server RDIMMs will start at 12.8 GT/s and scale to 14.4 GT/s and beyond, against DDR5's 9.2 GT/s ceiling. The data bus widens from 64 to 96 bits, split into four 24-bit sub-channels.

Tom's Hardware calculates up to 153.6 GB/s per module at baseline, four times DDR5's launch figure. DDR6 doubles the bank count and supports 128Gb dies with stacking. Tom's Hardware says RDIMMs could potentially reach 1TB or more per slot.

JEDEC calls DDR6 "built for the data center," with AI inferencing in mind. It lists RDIMM, UDIMM and CAMM as possible form factors. There is no launch date. Tom's Hardware points to 2029, while PC Gamer cites a 2028 to 2029 window.
key_points: DDR6 modules measure 74mm, 44 percent shorter than DDR5's 133mm, with a 96-bit data bus.
Server RDIMMs start at 12.8 GT/s, versus DDR5's 9.2 GT/s top speed, with 14.4 GT/s and beyond planned.
JEDEC says DDR6 is built for the data center; no launch date has been announced.

sources.name: PHP.net
sources.title: PHP 8.6 released with partial function application and new Duration class

stories.headline: PHP 8.6 ships partial function application and a Duration class
stories.dek: The release also adds a cross-platform polling API for many streams, a clamp() function, a SortDirection enum and structured stream errors.
stories.body:
PHP 8.6 is out, bringing partial function application, a new Duration class, a polling API and a clamp() function, according to PHP.net. Partial application lets developers supply some of a function's arguments in advance using ? and ... placeholders. The result is a Closure that runs once the remaining arguments arrive.

The \Time\Duration class represents elapsed time independent of any timezone. It covers more than 250 years with nanosecond precision and is aimed at timeouts and benchmark timings. The new Io\Poll API monitors many streams at once using epoll, kqueue, event ports or WSAPoll, avoiding the scalability limits of stream_select(). PHP.net says it is meant as a foundation for event loop libraries such as ReactPHP and AMPHP.

Other additions include a built-in SortDirection enum, stream operations that can throw a StreamException instead of emitting warnings, and default values for readonly properties.
key_points: PHP 8.6 adds partial function application using ? and ... placeholders that return a Closure.
The new Duration class spans more than 250 years with nanosecond precision.
Io\Poll uses epoll, kqueue, event ports or WSAPoll to watch many streams without stream_select() limits.
